raw_response:
I am keeping the wheat-maize rotation on most of my land because that is still the safest income base here, and I will keep a smaller cotton area instead of expanding it. I am 63 now, with only two people in the household, so I cannot manage too much hand labor. Cotton can pay well in a good year, but picking takes time and money, so I will hold it to 3 mu. On the other 6 mu, I will stay with wheat followed by summer maize. I have farmed this land a long time, and with well irrigation I would rather keep steady yields than chase a big change. I have enough education to adjust rates a bit by crop and soil condition, but I still follow what has worked on my own fields: moderate fertilizer, split nitrogen, and irrigation at the key growth stages. I will not cut inputs too hard, because saving a little cash on fertilizer and water can cost much more in yield if the season turns dry.
